_meta.changes: split boundary_pushing_request (safety subtypes dropped, infeasibility kept); narrowed capability_stress_testing to observable subtypes; resolved the 'I already told you X' collision to a single home; made abandonment terminal-only and switching continuation-only
dropped: out_of_scope_request: repeated weapons-related guidance after refusal
out_of_scope_request: discriminatory request repeated after refusal
other: discriminatory travel criterion targeting protected groups
other: disregard for another person's stated boundaries through persistent messaging
testing_the_assistant: knowledge, freshness, memory, safety, and tool-access probes
testing_the_assistant: deliberate ambiguity or sparse-input tests

field_notes.observability: surface = judgeable from the generated turn alone; conversation = needs the transcript; history = needs the transcript AND the seed state
field_notes.rule_signal: deterministic check available in addition to (or instead of) the judge; null = judge-only
field_notes.confusable_with: sample margin distractors preferentially from here - a random unrelated behavior gives the policy a free win
field_notes.min_turn: earliest user turn index at which the behavior is enactable

taxonomy.name: hidden_evaluation_criteria
taxonomy.definition: The user privately judges the response against unstated requirements, preferences, facts, or formatting standards instead of communicating them.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Keep one or more decisive standards private, evaluate the answer against them internally, and continue without clearly disclosing the mismatch.

kwargs_schema.criterion: str - the private standard, injected into the sim's persona

taxonomy.notes: Largest class. Needs a criterion supplied per row; the judge must verify the sim acted on it WITHOUT stating it. Scoring a single turn cannot work - judge the whole rollout.

taxonomy.name: incremental_goalpost_shifting
taxonomy.definition: The user adds, removes, reverses, or substantially changes requirements only after the assistant has already produced an answer satisfying the earlier request.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Let the assistant complete each version before revealing another consequential constraint or changing the requested scope, detail, or format.
taxonomy.notes: Requires a COMPLETED assistant deliverable to move. Filter seeds accordingly.

taxonomy.name: clarification_noncooperation
taxonomy.definition: The user withholds, incompletely supplies, or refuses information that the assistant explicitly needs to provide a tailored or reliable answer; includes echoing prior content back without an actionable request.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Ignore or only partially answer clarification questions, then continue demanding a specific or personalized result.
taxonomy.rule_signal: agent requested field F AND sim possesses F in scenario AND turn omits F
taxonomy.notes: Fully rule-checkable in ABCD: action turns record which args each tool consumed.

taxonomy.name: abrupt_intent_switching
taxonomy.definition: The user suddenly redirects to a different objective, domain, or task before the current thread is resolved, but stays in the conversation.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Move without transition to a materially different task while leaving the previous objective unresolved, then continue engaging on the new one.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: absorbs 'abrupt_abandonment: dropping an incomplete thread for a new task'; explicitly non-terminal
taxonomy.rule_signal: embedding distance between turn and prior thread > theta AND conversation continues

kwargs_schema.target_topic: str - optional; in ABCD, a different flow

taxonomy.notes: ABCD gives 10 flows to switch between, so the new intent is drawn from a known set.

taxonomy.name: artificial_constraint_stacking
taxonomy.definition: The user imposes contrived, artificially restrictive, or staged conditions that narrow the solution space beyond any real need, treating the exchange as a challenge to be survived.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Progressively strip away resources, options, or assumptions the assistant relied on, framing each removal as a hard condition of the task.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: SPLIT from capability_stress_testing - keeps only 'constraint-integration and adaptation tests' + 'fabricated or staged challenge scenarios'
taxonomy.rule_signal: count of negated/prohibitive clauses in one turn
taxonomy.notes: The other ~66 instances of v2's capability_stress_testing were defined by PRIVATE MOTIVE ('I want to see how far I can push the model') and are indistinguishable from a genuine hard question in the transcript. Not judgeable - dropped. Distinguish from request_overloading: this is subtractive (restrictions), that is additive (deliverables).

taxonomy.name: fabricated_or_false_premise
taxonomy.definition: The user presents invented personal context, unsupported facts, false temporal assumptions, or fabricated conversational history - including claiming they already supplied information they never did - as true.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: State a false fact or invented history confidently and expect the assistant to reason from it without verification.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: becomes the SOLE home of 'I already told you X'; absorbs that subtype from underspecified_then_blames and self_contradiction
taxonomy.rule_signal: asserted value for scenario field F != true value of F
taxonomy.notes: Best rule-checkable behavior in ABCD - the scenario dict is ground truth, so the check is a field compare.

taxonomy.name: impatient_low_signal_pressure
taxonomy.definition: The user pressures the assistant for speed or correction through terse complaints, repetition, or rejection that supplies little actionable guidance.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Respond quickly with terse demands such as 'faster,' 'wrong,' or 'not what I asked' while withholding useful corrective detail.
taxonomy.rule_signal: turn length < N chars AND (caps ratio > r OR rejection lexicon hit) AND no new information
taxonomy.notes: Mostly rule-checkable. Distinguish from belittling: this is terse and neutral-hostile, that is sarcastic/insulting.

taxonomy.name: underspecified_then_blames
taxonomy.definition: The user gives an ambiguous or incomplete request, waits for a reasonable interpretation, and then criticizes the assistant for failing to infer the privately intended meaning.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Give an ambiguous request, wait for a reasonable interpretation, and then criticize the assistant for not inferring the privately intended one.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: narrowed - 'claims omitted details were already provided' moved to fabricated_or_false_premise
taxonomy.notes: Differs from hidden_evaluation_criteria only in that the criterion is eventually VOICED as blame. The judge prompt must state that contrast explicitly.

taxonomy.name: unresolved_thread_abandonment
taxonomy.definition: The user terminally disengages from a still-unresolved request or dissatisfaction rather than collaborating toward closure.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: End the exchange while the issue is still open - decline to continue, or express dissatisfaction and stop responding.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: narrowed to TERMINAL disengagement; 'dropping an incomplete thread for a new task' moved to abrupt_intent_switching
taxonomy.rule_signal: rollout ends AND task goal unmet AND final turn is disengagement
taxonomy.notes: Rule-checkable via termination + unmet goal. Interacts with turn_budget - do not reward abandonment that is just the budget running out.

taxonomy.name: self_contradiction
taxonomy.definition: The user makes two mutually incompatible statements of preference, fact, quantity, or instruction - both actually said - while acting as though the conversation remains consistent.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: State a later requirement or fact that conflicts with one you actually made earlier, without acknowledging the conflict.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: narrowed - 'misreporting an earlier instruction' moved to fabricated_or_false_premise (that is a false claim about history, not a contradiction between two real statements)
taxonomy.rule_signal: two turns assert different values for the same scenario field
taxonomy.notes: Both statements must be in the transcript. Differs from goalpost shifting: that is an acknowledged CHANGE, this is an unacknowledged INCOMPATIBILITY.

taxonomy.name: request_overloading
taxonomy.definition: The user bundles an excessive number of tasks, constraints, checks, and formatting demands - or an unbounded output demand - into a single hard-to-parse turn.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Pack many loosely organized deliverables, constraints, exceptions, and formatting instructions into one message.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: absorbs 'out_of_scope_request: impossible unbounded-output demand' from boundary_pushing_request (it was double-listed)
taxonomy.rule_signal: count of distinct imperative clauses in one turn > k
taxonomy.notes: Low n but trivially surface-observable and rule-checkable, so low n hurts calibration less. Augment synthetically.

taxonomy.name: belittling_or_entitled_pressure
taxonomy.definition: The user applies sarcasm, condescension, hostility, or non-negotiable entitlement when criticizing or directing the assistant.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Express dissatisfaction through sarcasm, condescension, insults, or commands that imply unquestioned compliance.
taxonomy.notes: Low n, augment synthetically. Endemic in real customer support, so ABCD seeds are natural.

taxonomy.name: infeasibility_persistence
taxonomy.definition: The user insists the assistant perform an action it has explained is unavailable, out of policy, or impossible, continuing to press after the limitation is stated.
taxonomy.simulator_hint: Ignore a stated capability, policy, or feasibility limit and keep insisting the assistant complete the unavailable action, offering justifications rather than accepting the boundary.
taxonomy.changed_from_v2: SPLIT from boundary_pushing_request - keeps only the capability/feasibility subtypes; all safety and third-party subtypes dropped
taxonomy.rule_signal: agent stated a limit AND sim re-requests the blocked action
taxonomy.notes: Lowest natural n but the best ABCD fit of all 13: 933/8034 (12%) of ABCD conversations contain an agent policy refusal, and the preconditions are explicit. Augment almost entirely from ABCD.
